summary: Bohnanza is a card-trading game where you plant and harvest bean cards for coins, but the real game is the constant table talk and negotiation over trades. It's chaotic, social, and shines most as a loud party-ish game with a full table.
praised: Negotiation and trading is genuinely fun and social
Very easy to teach and explain
criticised: Can get chaotic and loud with experienced traders
Runtime can drag at higher player counts
Luck of the draw can hurt players who can't rearrange their hand

interaction.kind: direct card trading and negotiation with other players every turn
interaction.detail: The entire engine of the game runs on players negotiating trades of bean cards with each other, so what you can plant and harvest is constantly shaped by what others agree to give you or refuse to. There's essentially no private board — hands, trades, and the shared planting fields are all interaction surfaces.
interaction.said: "you can't win without trading," often called a negotiation/trading classic, sometimes joked about as a "friendship-ending" game because of the haggling

sources: coins from harvesting bean fields (per bean-type payout table)
scoring.how_you_win: Once the draw deck has been exhausted for the third time, whoever has accumulated the most gold coins from harvested bean fields wins.
